summary: The root أذي primarily signifies harm, hurt, or annoyance, whether physical or mental.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: aor. اَ َىَ, inf. n. أَ ًى, (T, M, Msb, K,) in [some of] the copies of the K written أَ ًا, and so by IB, (TA,) and أَ َآءٌ, (CK, [but not found by me in any MS. copy of the K nor in any other lexicon,]) and, accord. to IB, أَ َاةٌ and أَ ِيَّةٌ, (TA,) or these two are simple substs.; (M, K;) and; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) [ He was, or became, annoyed, molested, harmed, or hurt; ] he experienced, or suffered, slight evil, [i.

signifies فَعَلَ الأَ َى [ He did what annoyed, molested, harmed, or hurt ]. (M, K.) And آ ِاهُ, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) aor. يُؤْ ِيهِ, (S,) inf. n. إِي َآءٌ (T, IB, Msb) and [quasi-inf. n.] أَ ِيَّةٌ, (T,) or أَ َّى and أَ َاةٌ and أَ ِيَّةٌ, (S, K,) but IB refuses his assent to this, saying that these three are inf. ns.

inf. n. of 1. (T, M, Msb, K.) [As a simple subst., A state of annoyance or molestation. ] And [ Annoyance, molestation, harm, or hurt: quasi-] inf. n. of آ َاهُ. (S, K.) It signifies also, [like and,] كُلُّ مَا تَأْ َّيْتَ [ Anything by which thou art annoyed, molested, harmed, or hurt ]; (T;) or مَا يُؤْ ِيكَ [ a thing that annoys, molests, harms, or hurts thee ]: (Mgh:) or a slight evil; less than what is termed ضَرَر.

Experiencing, or suffering, [ annoyance, molestation, harm, hurt, or] what is disagreeable, or hateful, or evil, (M, * K, * Msb,) in a great, or vehement, degree; (M, K;) applied to a man; (M, Msb;) as also: (M, K:) and both signify the contr.; i. e. doing what is disagreeable, or hateful, or evil, in a great, or vehement, degree.
: and إِ ًا: see art. ا ا.
an inf. n. of 1. (IB.) And [quasi-] inf. n. of آ َاهُ. (S, K.) See also أَ َّي and أَ ِيَّةٌ.
and أَ ِيَّةٌ as its fem.: see أَ ٍ, in three places.

an inf. n. of 1. (IB.) And [quasi-] inf. n. of آ َاهُ. (S, K.) And a subst. from آ َاهُ; (Msb;) or, as also, a subst. from أَ ِىَ and تَأَ َّى; (M, K;) signifying A thing that is disagreeable, or hateful, or evil, in a small degree. (K.) See also أَ ًى.

(S, M, K, &c.,) with medd and teshdeed, (TA, [in the CK, erroneously, اَ ِىّ,]) Waves (S, M, K) of the sea: (S:) or vehement waves: (TA:) or the أَطْبَاق [app. meaning rollers, because they fall over like folds,] which the wind raises from the surface of the water, less than ( دُونَ [but this sometimes signifies above ]) what are termed مَوْج: (ISh, TA:) pl. أَوَا ِىُّ. (S.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
